label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa contra gentiles I.28… supports Whatever lives is more noble than any…
note: SCG I.28 [4], read against [1]'s comparison of living with merely existing things: merely existing things participate being in a particular and very imperfect mode. That bears on this premise. Gaps: [1] speaks of more perfect (excellence), not 'more noble' as the quarta via's respect; the claim's statement is the participation thesis, not the comparison; the universal over every living thing and every non-living actual thing is not stated; Pegis English basis.
